findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public service-provider interface, so implementations can exist outside this repository and may already be compiled against the previous version. Adding abstract order() makes those providers fail source compilation when rebuilt and throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration invokes order() at runtime. Give this method a default implementation (for example, returning 0) so existing providers remain binary and source compatible.

findings.title: Equal-priority crypto providers are selected in ServiceLoader order
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider are all assigned order 200. Comparator sorting preserves the unspecified ServiceLoader encounter order for equal values, and this code now silently selects the first provider instead of rejecting multiple providers as it did previously. Consequently, a classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS providers can nondeterministically initialize a non-FIPS provider, undermining the intended cryptographic mode. Reject ties for the highest priority or assign priorities that make the selection unambiguous.
